cbse-9-science-describing-motion-around-.subject: Science
notes: Chapter Overview
Motion is described by how an object's position changes with time relative to a reference point.
Reference Point
An object is considered moving when its position changes with time relative to a chosen observer or reference point.
Distance
Distance is the total length of the path travelled. It is a scalar quantity and is never negative.
Displacement
Displacement is the directed change from initial to final position. It depends only on the start and end positions.
Speed
Average speed = total distance ÷ total time. Speed tells how fast an object covers distance, without direction.
Velocity
Average velocity = displacement ÷ time. Velocity includes direction, so it can be positive, negative or zero according to the chosen direction.
Acceleration
Acceleration measures change in velocity with time. a = (v-u)/t. A negative sign indicates direction relative to the chosen positive direction.
Graphs
The slope of a position-time graph gives velocity. The slope of a velocity-time graph gives acceleration. The area under a velocity-time graph gives displacement for the interval.
Constant Acceleration
For straight-line motion with constant acceleration: v=u+at, s=ut+½at², and v²=u²+2as.
Units
Use SI units where possible: metre (m), second (s), metre per second (m/s), metre per second squared (m/s²).
qa: What is motion?
Motion is a change in position with time relative to a reference point.
Why is a reference point needed?
Rest and motion are described relative to an observer or reference point.
Differentiate distance and displacement.
Distance is total path length; displacement is the directed change from initial to final position.
Define average speed.
Average speed is total distance divided by total time.
Define average velocity.
Average velocity is displacement divided by total time.
What is acceleration?
Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with time.
Can displacement be zero when distance is not zero?
Yes. On returning to the starting point, displacement is zero while distance travelled is non-zero.
What does the slope of a position-time graph represent?
Velocity.
What does the slope of a velocity-time graph represent?
Acceleration.
What does the area under a velocity-time graph represent?
Displacement over the relevant time interval.

cbse-9-mathematics-orienting-yourself.subject: Mathematics
cbse-9-mathematics-orienting-yourself.chapter: Orienting Yourself: The Use of Coordinates
notes: Chapter Overview
Coordinates give a precise way to describe the position of a point on a plane.
Coordinate Plane
Two perpendicular number lines form the coordinate plane: the horizontal x-axis and vertical y-axis.
Origin
The point where the two axes meet is the origin, written as (0,0).
Ordered Pair
A point is written (x,y). The x-coordinate is read first and the y-coordinate second.
Axes
A point on the x-axis has y=0. A point on the y-axis has x=0.
Signs
Positive x means right, negative x means left; positive y means up, negative y means down.
Quadrants
The axes divide the plane into four quadrants. The signs of x and y help identify the quadrant.
Plotting
To plot a point, start at the origin, move along x first and then along y.
Reading Coordinates
Always read coordinates in the fixed order (x,y); swapping the numbers generally changes the point.
Common Mistake
Do not reverse x and y and do not ignore the negative sign.
qa: What is the origin?
The origin is the intersection of the x-axis and y-axis, written (0,0).
What is an ordered pair?
An ordered pair (x,y) is a fixed-order pair of numbers used to locate a point.
Which coordinate is read first?
The x-coordinate is read first.
When does a point lie on the x-axis?
When its y-coordinate is zero.
When does a point lie on the y-axis?
When its x-coordinate is zero.
How do you plot (3,-2)?
Move 3 units right from the origin, then 2 units down.
Why is order important?
Because (a,b) and (b,a) normally represent different points.
What does a negative x-coordinate mean?
The point lies to the left of the y-axis.
What does a positive y-coordinate mean?
The point lies above the x-axis.
How many quadrants are formed by the axes?
Four.

cbse-6-science-wonderful-world.subject: Science
notes: Chapter Overview
Science begins with curiosity and uses careful observation, questions, evidence and reasoning to understand the world.
Observation
Observe carefully using senses and suitable tools; record what you actually notice.
Questions
A useful investigation begins with a clear question that can be explored using observations or measurements.
Evidence
Evidence is information collected from observations, measurements or investigations that supports or challenges an idea.
Fair Test
Change one main factor while keeping other important conditions as similar as practical.
Measurement
Use an appropriate instrument and unit when a quantity can be measured.
Observation vs Explanation
'The leaf is green' is an observation; 'the leaf is green because...' is an explanation that needs evidence.
Recording Data
Tables, labelled diagrams and simple lists help make observations easier to compare.
Conclusion
A conclusion should match the evidence collected rather than simply repeat a guess.
Science in Daily Life
Scientific thinking helps explain familiar phenomena in cooking, weather, plants, animals, materials and technology.
qa: What is observation?
Observation is careful noticing and recording of information using senses and suitable tools.
Why do scientists ask questions?
Questions define what needs to be investigated and what evidence should be collected.
What is evidence?
Evidence is information gathered through observations, measurements or tests.
What is a fair test?
A comparison in which important conditions are kept controlled while the main factor under study is changed.
Why record measurements?
Recorded measurements allow comparison, analysis and checking later.
Give an example of an observation.
Example: The water level in a beaker changed from 100 mL to 80 mL.
Why repeat observations?
Repeating can make evidence more reliable and help identify accidental errors.
What should a conclusion be based on?
The evidence collected during the investigation.
Why is a ruler useful?
It provides a standard way to measure length.
What is a testable question?
A question that can be investigated through observation, measurement or a fair test.
